subject: radiology
title: Drain aftercare: tubes, skin and freedom

steps.tx: Regular flushing keeps a drainage lumen open and working on the ward. **Daily gentle flushing** with small saline volumes clears debris without bursting the tract. **Output charts** record colour and volume and detect a failing tube early. Secure dressings and **fixation checks** prevent the tube from pulling out during movement. Families learn to keep the drainage bag below the entry level at all times so fluid drains freely.
steps.say: Regular flushing keeps a drainage lumen open and working on the ward. Gentle daily saline clears debris without bursting the tract during care. Output charts are useful because they record colour and volume and detect failure. Secure fixation prevents pull out, and families keep bags below entry level so fluid drains freely.

steps.tx: Planned exchanges prevent sudden blockage of long term drainage tubes. **Scheduled tube swaps** every few months clear crusts before occlusion strands an organ. The tract is inspected at each exchange so **granulation tissue** and infection are spotted early. Upsizing a narrowed tract restores flow where downsizing previously served healing. A tube is removed when **free internal flow** is proven and the underlying disease has resolved.
steps.say: Planned exchanges prevent sudden blockage of long term drainage tubes. Scheduled swaps clear crusts before occlusion strands an organ without drainage. Inspection at exchange is valuable because it spots granulation and infection early. A tube is removed when internal flow is proven and the underlying disease has resolved fully.

steps.tx: Skin around a leaking tube needs active protection and regular review. **Barrier creams** with well sealed bags protect skin bathed in bile or urine. A **peritubal leak** may mean a loose track that needs upsizing or infection that needs treatment. Overgrown **granulation tissue** from chronic irritation can be trimmed with silver nitrate application. A dressing allergy can mimic infection and needs a change of tape and careful reassessment.
steps.say: Skin around a leaking tube needs active protection and regular review. Barrier creams with sealed bags protect skin bathed in bile or urine. A leak may mean a loose track or infection and needs careful assessment. Granulation tissue can be trimmed, while dressing allergy mimics infection and needs a tape change.

steps.tx: A capping trial proves internal drainage before the bag is finally removed. **Capping and clamping** close the external route and test whether fluid passes internally. Observation after removal detects reblockage early through fever, pain or falling output. Clinic review with imaging confirms **lasting patency** after the tube is removed. A **red flag card** tells the family when falling output, fever or leakage needs urgent return.
steps.say: A capping trial proves internal drainage before the bag is finally removed. Capping closes the external route and tests internal passage properly. Observation after removal is important because it detects reblockage through fever and pain. A warning card tells the family when falling output or leakage needs urgent return to hospital.

steps.tx: The photograph shows a dressed abdominal drain with a blue **clamp** closed on the tube during a capping trial. The tube end is capped, so bile or urine must pass internally if drainage is adequate. The patient holds a **red flag card** that lists fever, rigors, flank pain and leakage as warning signs. This image teaches that **tube removal** follows proven flow and clear safety advice.
